reviews.review:
Immortal: Unchained is better than reviews could make one expect. The final product is a pretty solid B-Side Souls-like, in line with Hellpoint. On top of that it has the added unusual aspect of being a shooter as opposed to a melee adventure. In the end, Immortal feels akin to Remnant from the Ashes, including some of the world-building itself.

This is of course not to say Immortal is without faults. It is a little bit buggier than is preferable. There can be issues with aiming at enemies close to you and bullets not going where you would like, or getting stuck in the terrain once or twice, and a couple of menu bugs that just mean you have to press escape to exit instead of clicking. Special attacks with most weapons seem largely ineffective, and there's only some colour changes available to fulfil your fashion needs. With another pass of bug fixing/polish most of these problems would probably disappear.

One of the biggest issues with the game may lie in retreading ground to open chests. This isn't like a Zelda game and with a new ability you can now access that frozen chest you've walked past a couple of times. This is finding chests all over that require increasing numbers of a key, and occasionally some special keys. They all look the same, and often you don't have enough of the keys or the special key until you've gone through two other zones, and there is no reason for you to return besides these chests, and a handful of doors throughout the entire game that are at least more memorable. The game would probably be better without the hassle. On top of that, ability to teleport to anywhere you've been already is limited not only by needing to pay to unlock the obelisk, but needing to get through a third of the game before you -can- unlock them. So if you want to retread any of that area, you have to go through all of it again.

Pretty solid/10. Also whichever monster said snipers were terrible was wrong.
